 Nebula brings ‘Jet Lag: The Game’ back to the big screen for season 20 with international theatrical event across the U.S., the U.K. and Canada
 November 5, 2026 
 The 90-minute theatrical premiere of “Hide + Seek: Italy” will screen across more than 160 theatres at Regal, Picturehouse, Cineworld and Landmark locations on December 5; select theatres will feature exclusive pre-show trivia; tickets go on sale November 5 
 NEW YORK (Thursday, November 5) – Nebula, the largest creator-owned and operated independent media company, today announced that its hit original series Jet Lag: The Game will return to theatres for a special theatrical premiere of its 20th season, Hide + Seek: Italy , on December 5. In partnership with Regal, Picturehouse, Cineworld and Landmark Cinemas across the U.S., U.K., and Canada, the 90-minute theatrical presentation will screen across more than 160 theatre screens in three countries, giving fans an opportunity to experience the series together on the big screen. Select theatres will also feature an on-screen trivia experience ahead of the special presentation, bringing an additional interactive element to the theatrical event. Tickets go on sale Thursday, November 5.
 “The magic of Jet Lag is the community, so it’s a real joy to work with our friends at Picturehouse, Regal, Cineworld, and Landmark to bring that community together in the real world,” said Dave Wiskus, Founder of Nebula.
 “Our first Jet Lag: The Game theatrical event demonstrated the potential of bringing an established digital audience into the movie theatre. Nebula has built one of the most engaged fanbases in the creator space, and that enthusiasm translated directly into theatrical demand. Hide + Seek Italy builds on that momentum, and we look forward to welcoming fans back to experience the series together on the big screen,” said Brooks LeBoeuf, Senior Vice President of U.S. Content at Regal.
 In Hide + Seek: Italy , the 20th season of Jet Lag: The Game , the boys face off in a six-day game of Hide + Seek across Italy, exploring its scenic seaside towns, medieval mountain villages and rolling Roman hills. But this season is no vacation: the classic Hide + Seek format has been elevated to “Expert Mode,” removing the game’s most powerful questions and introducing new mechanics designed to punish seekers for making mistakes. In the season premiere, Ben and Adam grapple with the new Expert Mode questions as Sam relaxes on the beach.
 The upcoming event builds on the growing success of Jet Lag: The Game ’s theatrical presence. In August 2026, the series brought its Japanorama season premiere to Picturehouse Cinemas in London for a special theatrical event, followed by an international rollout of the Season 19 finale across Regal, Picturehouse and Cineworld locations in October. The response to these events demonstrated the enthusiasm of the series’ passionate fan community and the appeal of experiencing the competition together in theatres. The Season 20 event marks the largest international theatrical footprint for the series to date.

 About Nebula
 Nebula is the largest creator-owned and operated media company, built across three integrated business units: Nebula Studios, Nebula Talent, and Nebula Streaming. Nebula Studios develops and produces premium original content, extending creator voices into prestige storytelling across digital and traditional media. Nebula Talent partners with leading independent creators, supporting their growth through brand partnerships, audience development, and long-term career strategy. Nebula Streaming is a premium subscription platform featuring exclusive, original, and ad-free programming from some of the world’s most influential independent creators. Together, these divisions form a unified ecosystem where creators can develop, produce, and distribute their work on their own terms. As one of the leading creator-owned media platforms, Nebula champions ambitious, creator-driven storytelling and provides sustainable pathways for independent voices to expand from digital platforms into film, television, and other premium entertainment formats.
 About Regal Global Entertainment
 Regal Global Entertainment operates the second-largest theatrical exhibition business in the world with 7,648 screens across 629 locations. Through its Cinema City, Cineworld, Picturehouse, Planet, and Regal brands, the company is committed to delivering exceptional moviegoing experiences through premium large formats, innovative loyalty and subscription programs, enhanced food and beverage offerings, and outstanding guest service.
 About Picturehouse
 Picturehouse is an award-winning UK film company incorporating cinema, distribution and home entertainment, formed in 1989 to challenge the multiplex model. Its flagship cinema Picturehouse Central is situated in the heart of London’s West End, with the rest of its 25 venues located across England and Scotland. Picturehouse’s architecturally unique cinemas sit in the heart of local neighbourhoods and cater to a diverse and wide-ranging audience. They provide bespoke food and drink offerings across their cafés, bars, restaurants, and members’ bars. The programme is curated to champion films made for all ages and backgrounds, from quality mainstream film through to foreign-language and documentary features, as well as live event cinema and in-person events and Q&As when available.
